set system host-name [parameter1].explanation: Configure the host name of the device.

parameters.name: hostname
parameters.explanation: The host name of the equipment is used to identify the equipment in the network.

unit [parameter2] family inet address [p.explanation: Configure IPv4 addresses for interfaces and subnet masks.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.explanation: Interface unit number to distinguish between multiple logical configurations under the same interface.

parameters.name: ip-address
parameters.explanation: The IPv4 address assigned to the interface.

unit [parameter2] tunnel source [paramet.explanation: Configure the tunnel source address for the interface.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.explanation: Interface unit number to distinguish between multiple logical configurations under the same interface.

parameters.name: source-interface
parameters.explanation: Tunnel source interface name, e.g. lo0.0.

unit [parameter2] encapsulation [paramet.explanation: Configure the containment type of the interface.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.explanation: Interface unit number to distinguish between multiple logical configurations under the same interface.

unit [parameter2] tunnel destination [pa.explanation: Configure the tunnel address for the interface to be dynamic.

parameters.name: unit
parameters.explanation: Interface unit number to distinguish between multiple logical configurations under the same interface.

set security ipsec vpn [parameter1].explanation: This command configures an IPsec VPN in Junos by setting specific parameters (e.g., name, IKE gateway, IPsec policy) under the `security ipsec vpn` hierarchy.

bind-interface [parameter2].explanation: Tie IPSec VPN to the specified interface.

parameters.name: bind-interface
parameters.explanation: The name of the bound interface, e.g. g-1/0/0.0.

parameters.name: router-id
parameters.explanation: Router ID of equipment for OSPF, BGP, etc.

set protocols ospf area [parameter1].explanation: This command configures an OSPF area in Junos OS, where `[parameter1]` specifies the area ID, enabling OSPF routing within the defined area.
